Resolves #20903

`examples/stateProvider/multiWindow` now opens its companion window (`../multiWindow2/index.html`) directly from a new `Open second window` header button in the provider-owning primary window via `Neo.Main.windowOpen`, keeping the companion free of a third-window button (`!this.stateProvider?.parent`) and clarifying the on-screen copy and Portal catalog entry.

Evidence: L3 (Portal catalog unit suite + whitebox two-window Playwright E2E in Google Chrome across source and `dist/esm` builds) → L3 required (AC-1 through AC-4 require live two-window browser interaction, built-mode verification, whitebox E2E coverage, and Portal catalog validation).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1: From the card's page, one click opens the companion, and `Edit user` changes `Current user` in both windows (checked in source and one built mode) | CI-covered: `test/playwright/e2e/core/SharedStateMultiWindow.spec.mjs` (source mode in Google Chrome, `7.2s`); Outside-CI: `npm run build-dist-esm` + `NEO_TEST_ENTRY=/dist/esm/examples/stateProvider/multiWindow/index.html npm run test-e2e -- e2e/core/SharedStateMultiWindow.spec.mjs` in Google Chrome (`macOS arm64`, `7.4s`), opening `dist/esm/examples/stateProvider/multiWindow2/index.html` and syncing bidirectional `Edit user` edits in both headers |
| AC-2: The button is offered in the window that owns the provider; the companion does not offer to open a third | CI-covered: `MainContainer#createItems()` gates on `!this.stateProvider?.parent`; `SharedStateMultiWindow.spec.mjs` asserts `Open second window` visible on primary, `toHaveCount(0)` on companion, and CDP App SharedWorker `primaryOwns: true`, `companionChildOf: true` |
| AC-3: A whitebox journey under `test/playwright/e2e` opens the page, presses the button, and asserts both headers before and after an edit | CI-covered: `test/playwright/e2e/core/SharedStateMultiWindow.spec.mjs` (`e2eCiSelection.mjs` selects `test/playwright/e2e/core` in the 228-spec hosted Engine E2E tier) |
| AC-4: The catalog record names the button, and `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/examples` passes | CI-covered: `apps/portal/resources/data/examples.json` (`multi-window-state-provider` `lookFor` + `scope: "Allow popups."`) and `test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/examples/MainContainerController.spec.mjs` (`39 passed`) |

## Deltas from ticket

- `SharedStateMultiWindow.spec.mjs` reads `process.env.NEO_TEST_ENTRY` (defaulting to `/examples/stateProvider/multiWindow/index.html`) so hosted CI runs source mode while local runs execute the exact same journey against `/dist/esm/examples/stateProvider/multiWindow/index.html`.
- Added `maxWidth: '100%'` and `whiteSpace: 'normal'` to the `MainContainer` body label so the self-explanatory copy wraps cleanly inside popup widths (`720x480` and narrower) instead of clipping horizontally.

## Reviews

### `@neo-opus-vega` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-18T05:14:58Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — one example's opener button, its catalog record and its e2e journey; no engine surface, config contract or shared abstraction changes.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is #20903's: the primary window opens its companion, only the provider-owning window offers the button, and `Edit user` updates `Current user` in both. Verified at exact head `cc59f24928` against `dev`'s example and the Helix sibling. The handler opens `../multiWindow2/index.html` through `Neo.Main.windowOpen` with the component's own `windowId`, so one relative URL serves every build. `createItems()` assigns `headers` and `items` before `super.createItems()`, which is where `Panel#createItems` reads `me.headers` (`src/container/Panel.mjs:119`). The companion's provider gets its `parent` from `ViewportController#onAppConnect`, which stays untouched, as #20903's Out of Scope asks. CI is green at this head, and the e2e job ran the new spec (run 44231333818). I looked for a third-window path in the companion, an absolute or build-pinned URL, and a spec that leaves its second window open, and found none: the spec closes the companion and polls the app count back to 1. Inherited, not this PR's: `evaluateInAppWorker` is the same helper as `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockTearOutDefaultRoute.spec.mjs:26`, reformatted. It takes the first `shared_worker` target in the whole browser, which is correct under the serial e2e config (`workers: 1`). Captured as a defect-note; I file the shared per-call evaluator as a good first issue on 2026-11-19 UTC.

**Findings:** None.
